description: List the workspace's mail domains, oldest first. A mail domain is a name you claim on our mail servers: `inbox` gives your agents addresses on it, and `send` lets your app send transactional email from it. Each one lists the DNS records to create at your DNS provider (`records`, in the order to create them), with what the last check found for each (`check`). `status` is `pending` (you added it and its records are not all right yet; it ends on its own at `claimExpiresAt`), `active` (the records are right) or `failing` (it was active and a record broke; it keeps working until `graceEndsAt`). `waitingForUs` is true while our part of a record is not live yet: there is nothing for you to do. `heldElsewhere` is true when the records are right but another workspace holds the name. Once a domain is `active` or `failing`, `signing` names the key we sign its mail with: `selector`, and `since`, when it began. `rotating` is true while we switch to a new key, which needs nothing from you, because your DNS records stay as they are. `stopped` is true when the records failed past `graceEndsAt` and we stopped sending from the domain. While the domain is `pending`, `signing` is null. For an `inbox` domain, `receiving` is true once its MX record points at us. `mxMovedSince` is when a check first saw the MX stop pointing at us after it had, and goes back to null once the MX points at us again. For a `send` domain, `senderAddresses` is how many sender addresses it holds (list_sender_addresses lists them), and it is null for an `inbox` domain. For an active or failing sending domain, `ses` shows Amazon SES verification: `state` is `pending`, `verified` or `failed`; `dkimSelector` is the last signing key uploaded, `checkedAt` is the last check time, and `problem` says what failed and what to do. It is null for an inbox domain or an unproven claim. SES verification runs in the worker; checking DNS does not finish it. `tenant` says whether Amazon SES lets this workspace send: `state` is `enabled` or `paused`, and `since` is when that last changed. While it is `paused`, sends from its sender addresses are refused with 409 and nothing is sent from them; only our team turns it back on, after a review. It is null when we have no reading. `dmarc.from` names the domain that holds the DMARC record covering the name, which is the domain itself or one above it, and is null when no check found one. `ourPartAutomatic` is true once our system has written a record of ours on its own, so it adds the rest the same way. False means we have no proof yet, not that someone adds them by hand. While a domain is not active, `dnsHost` names the DNS provider that holds its zone, as list_tracking_domains describes. For a `send` domain that is `active` or `failing`, `reading` is its last `windowDays` days of mail, counted from `countedFrom`: `sent` emails that left our servers from its sender addresses, `bounced` of them that bounced for an address the receiver refused, and `complained` of them that a person marked as spam (only some mail servers tell us, so a low number is not proof). Once `sent` reaches `minSample`, we hold the domain's sender addresses when the share of `bounced` or of `complained` in `sent` reaches `pauseAt`, in percent. A bounce share holds only when it comes from at least `pauseBreadth.bounces` bounces to `pauseBreadth.recipientDomains` different receiving domains. A spam share holds only when at least `pauseComplainers` different people marked an email as spam; one person counts once. Below `minSample` there is no share to judge, so none is given. `policyHold` holds the counts that a receiving server's refusals as spam held the domain on, frozen when it was held, and is null otherwise. `review` is the hold on the domain, if one stands: the case number to quote, since when, why and the date we said we would review by. It is null while no hold stands. Send `kind` to list only one use.

kind.description: Only domains of this kind. Leave it out for both.
